$comment: UCL-000001 — Universal Constitutional Lifecycle. THIS FILE IS DATA AND RULES ONLY. It declares no stage, no stage name, no stage ordering, no capability and no capability name: every one of those is DISCOVERED. Adding a lifecycle stage, a canonical capability, a Canonical Knowledge Object kind, a relation type, a graph type, a metadata provider, a metadata adapter, a serialization, an obligation, a property or an expansion axis is an append-only edit to DATA and requires no change to ucl_engine.py (PR-07 Zero Enumeration). The engine holds no stage id, no capability name, no owner path, no graph type and no serialization parser choice.
$cko_comment: CANONICAL KNOWLEDGE OBJECT MODEL. Every constitutionally governed entity is normalized to a Canonical Knowledge Object (CKO): a kind, an identity, an owner, an authority, a provenance and a set of typed relations to other CKOs. Repository Truth is expressed as RELATIONSHIPS AMONG CKOs, never as an implementation-specific structure. The Discovery Engine reads CKOs and nothing else — it never sees a file, a format or a field name.
$pipeline_comment: DISCOVERY PIPELINE. Metadata Provider (WHERE constitutional metadata lives, and in which serialization) → Metadata Adapter (HOW that provider's records normalize into CKOs of a declared kind) → Canonical Knowledge Objects → Discovery Engine (composes graphs, evaluates obligations, orders and executes). Each arrow is data-declared. Replacing a serialization or a storage technology means registering a provider and an adapter; it changes no CKO kind, no relation type, no graph type, no obligation, no property and no stage.
$graph_comment: GRAPH COMPOSITION. Graph types are themselves CKO-declared and OPEN: `graph_types` is a registry, not a fixed set, and each type is composed by selecting CKO kinds as nodes and relation types as edges. The architecture assumes no permanently fixed set of graph types — appending a graph type is an append here.

programme.name: Universal Constitutional Lifecycle
programme.authority: NONE — DERIVED TRUTH. This programme legislates no lifecycle, opens no registry, mints no identifier, declares no namespace, admits no capability and certifies nothing. UCIC-001 owns the single deterministic lifecycle every capability follows; CEP-009 ADDENDUM B owns constitutional admission; ENG-001 D30 and UMB-003 §3 own the artifact lifecycle; UEI-000001 §17 owns the evolution lifecycle; 02-EXECUTION-LIFECYCLE.md owns the execution lifecycle. This programme DISCOVERS the constitutional stage graph those instruments already declare, normalizes it into Canonical Knowledge Objects, unifies it without merging its authorities, measures whether each stage is executable, and executes the discovered graph. Where this measurement and a located instrument differ, the located instrument governs.
programme.disclosure: **DISCLOSURE.** This programme holds no constitutional authority. It is not a second lifecycle, not a second registry, not a second dictionary, not a second identifier scheme and not a competing methodology. It creates no stage: every stage it reports is bound to a canonical owner the repository already legislated. It enumerates nothing: stages, capabilities, owners, authorities, obligations, dependencies, admission paths and graph types are discovered from Canonical Constitutional Metadata through providers and adapters. Ω-E04 implements the substrate; Ω-E05 (ACEE) executes it autonomously.
programme.$forbidden_write_comment: Every claimant this programme reads. A claimant it could write is a claimant it could silently reconcile, so --check-write-scope fails closed if its own home falls inside one of these and --check-declaration fails closed if a cited owner is left unprotected.

$cko_model_comment: The CKO kind registry and the relation type registry. Both are OPEN: a previously unknown constitutionally governed entity is admitted by appending a kind, and a previously unknown relationship by appending a relation type. Neither the engine nor any graph type needs to change.

cko_model.admission: Append a kind to `kinds` or a relation to `relation_types`. No engine change.

Nothing constitutional depends on which entry is used.

$adapters_comment: METADATA ADAPTERS — HOW a provider's records normalize into CKOs. `pointer` is a dotted path into the deserialized document (empty means the document root). `field_map` maps the CKO's neutral vocabulary onto whatever field names that provider happens to use; `relation_map` maps provider fields onto declared relation types. This is the layer that makes discovery independent of serialization AND of source schema. Adapter ids are the stable names other constitutional metadata refers to when it binds a stage to a counterpart.

$reference_normalization_comment: DECLARED reading rules for references written by other owners. A located record may name an instrument as an identifier prefix, or annotate it with a section or a parenthetical remark — `00-CEP/CEP-005`, `00-CEP/CEP-002 Art 28`, `engine/kernel (immutable baseline)`. Those are faithful references in a human-authored register, not defects, and this programme may not edit another owner's record to suit its parser. So the READING is declared instead: each rule is data, is applied in order, and the rule that resolved a reference is recorded as evidence. `prefix-unique` resolves only when exactly one located file matches, because resolving an ambiguous prefix would be this programme guessing what the owner meant.

reference_normalizations.note: A trailing parenthetical is an annotation on the reference, not part of the path.
A trailing section marker locates a place WITHIN the instrument; the instrument is the reference.
An instrument named by identifier prefix resolves to the unique located file whose name begins with it. Ambiguity is left unresolved rather than guessed.

$relationship_model_comment: RELATIONSHIPS ARE FIRST-CLASS. A relationship is itself a constitutionally governed entity, so it possesses its own Canonical Knowledge Object with its own immutable semantic identity. Graphs are therefore composed from entity CKOs AND relationship CKOs, not from entities plus untyped pointers. A relationship CKO records its participants as attributes rather than as further relations, which is what stops the model regressing infinitely while keeping the relationship itself governable.

relationship_model.$identity_comment: A relationship's constitutional identity is derived from the relation type and the SEMANTIC IDENTITIES of its participants — never from a handle, an adapter, a provider, a serialization or a path. A target that is a located artifact is resolved to its registered constitutional identity through the Universal Registry; a target the repository has deliberately not registered carries no constitutional identity, and that is REPORTED rather than patched with its path, because a path is a location and locations may evolve.
relationship_model.note: The relation TYPE registry is declared in cko_model.relation_types and is open; each relationship INSTANCE is discovered through the same provider and adapter pipeline as an entity, and carries the provenance of the metadata that declared it.

$semantic_identity_comment: SEMANTIC IDENTITY IS INVARIANT. Every CKO possesses exactly one immutable semantic identity, derived ONLY from what the entity IS — its kind and its recorded identity. Representation, serialization, storage, transport, runtime, implementation and LOCATION are excluded from the derivation by construction, so all of them may evolve without disturbing identity. An identifier may itself evolve through constitutional governance; what may never change under that evolution is that the entity has exactly one semantic identity, and --check-semantic-identity proves the derivation ignores every excluded input.

semantic_identity.$comment: Derived only from what the entity IS. Every input the invariants permit to evolve — representation, serialization, storage, transport, runtime, implementation and location — is excluded by construction, so none of them can mint a new identity. The inputs are read from this declaration, so the derivation is governed rather than hard-coded, and --check-semantic-identity proves no excluded input participates.

$knowledge_extraction_comment: KNOWLEDGE EXTRACTION. Every completed execution extracts engineering knowledge, and that knowledge becomes Canonical Knowledge Objects so it accumulates constitutionally across future cycles. Extraction is a measurement of the run, never an assertion about it. Registration is delegated to the LOCATED knowledge home: this programme opens no knowledge store, because Knowledge Once means the canonical home already exists and a second one would fork it. Each extraction record therefore names the owner that registers it, and readiness is measured rather than claimed.

$applicability_comment: OBLIGATION APPLICABILITY. An obligation is not universally applicable, and counting an inapplicable obligation as unbound would manufacture a deficiency the repository does not have. Every obligation therefore declares its applicability, and Repository Truth — not this declaration — decides the CONDITIONAL cases: the condition is itself a rule evaluated against discovered objects. Only REQUIRED obligations, and CONDITIONAL obligations whose condition is satisfied, participate in gate failure. NOT_APPLICABLE obligations are reported as such and never counted as unbound. Each condition below is deliberately non-circular: it asks whether the repository puts the stage in scope for the obligation, never whether the obligation is already met.

$execution_comment: The lifecycle EXECUTES the discovered graph. Execution is a deterministic constitutional traversal in topological order over lifecycle-stage CKOs: it resolves each stage's relations and obligations and emits a run record. It deliberately does NOT re-invoke the stages' own engines — those are already executed by the fixed-point pipeline, and invoking them from here would create the self-observation topology RFP-3 forbids and make the repository non-convergent. The run record is a pure function of the goal text and the discovered graph: no wall clock, no commit identity, no working-tree status.

findings.title: Property conformance is measured per stage and held at full coverage by a zero bound
findings.detail: The ten declared properties are evaluated per discovered stage against located metadata, and every stage currently exhibits every property. The bound is held at zero rather than removed, so the dimension is a RATCHET: if a future stage is admitted that does not exhibit a declared property, or a located instrument stops declaring what a property is measured from, the count rises above the bound and the gate closes. A dimension that only passed because nothing measured it would be the defect this programme exists to prevent.
findings.why_not_repaired: Nothing is presently divergent. The finding is retained because the bound must name a disposing finding to be admissible, and because the ratchet is the reason the bound is zero rather than absent.

findings.title: Four applicable obligations are unbound, each traced to a named cause in Repository Truth
findings.detail: Eleven obligations are evaluated against forty-five discovered stages. Applicability is determined first, so the inapplicable cases are reported rather than counted: registration is not applicable where the Universal Registry does not admit the zone the owner lives in — operational memory is deliberately barred from consuming a permanent corpus identity, so its absence from the registry is the exclusion authority working correctly — and replay and fixed-point proof are not applicable to a stage the repository declares constitutionally but does not execute. After applicability, exactly four obligations remain genuinely unbound. THREE belong to gap discovery: its owner lies in a zone that constitutional checks do cover, and the repository does execute it as a pipeline member, but no declared gate certifies, validates or verifies that artifact — so the obligation is in scope and unmet. ONE belongs to certification: it is a pipeline member, so replay is in scope, but the pipeline declares that stage non-reentrant as deliberate defence in depth against a recursion that would stop the repository converging. The bound equals the measured total exactly, so it carries no slack and any regression closes the gate.
findings.why_not_repaired: An obligation is bound by the located instrument that owns the stage, not by the measurement that reads it. Declaring a gate for gap discovery, or flipping the reentrancy of the certification stage, would amend another owner's record to improve this programme's own report — and in the second case would re-arm the exact recursion the pipeline documents itself as defending against. Each unbound obligation is reported against its stage and its owner in the obligation matrix, so the referral is specific rather than aggregate.

findings.title: The token UCL is recorded historically against rejected non-UCOS concepts
findings.detail: The assimilation register records identifiers UCL-001 through UCL-015 as NOT-UCOS, IDEA, HISTORICAL-EVIDENCE-ONLY, NO_CURRENT_FORM, dispositioned REJECT and RETAIN-AS-HISTORY. Those are concept identifiers in the assimilation concept space. This programme's home is UCL-000001 in the programme-home space and consumes no corpus identity at all, so the two do not collide; the coincidence is recorded here so a future reader does not mistake this programme for the rejected concepts or vice versa.
findings.why_not_repaired: Nothing is defective. Recorded history is never rewritten, and disambiguation is the appropriate remedy rather than a rename that would erase the historical record's usefulness.

findings.title: Some relationship targets carry no registered constitutional identity
findings.detail: A relationship's constitutional identity derives from the semantic identities of its participants. Where a target is a located artifact that the Universal Registry does not admit — overwhelmingly operational memory, which is deliberately barred from consuming a permanent corpus identity — the target has no registered constitutional identity to derive from. Those relationships are counted and reported. Their handles remain distinct, so no relationship is lost or conflated in the graph. The bound is a RATCHET held at exactly the measured value, so it is re-tightened whenever governed records are lawfully admitted. It moved from 92 to 98 when Ω-E05 declared PROGRAM-000021 in the aggregate certifier: that programme delegates to six located owners, every one of which is operational memory the registry deliberately does not admit, so each delegation is exactly this disclosed condition and not a new one. The delta was measured against the committed reading — six added, none removed — rather than assumed, and no other relationship moved.
findings.why_not_repaired: The remedy would be to substitute the target's PATH into the identity, and a path is a location that the invariants expressly permit to evolve — using it would convert a location change into an identity change, which is the defect this invariant exists to prevent. Registering operational memory to obtain an identity would instead violate the exclusion authority. The condition is therefore reported and referred to the registry owner.

$identity_handle_comment: IDENTITY VERSUS HANDLE. `cko_id` is a local HANDLE — it names the adapter that normalized the record, so it is an implementation characteristic and may change. `semantic_id` is the CONSTITUTIONAL IDENTITY and is derived exclusively from immutable constitutional identity fields. A digest is used, but only over those fields: a digest over anything mutable would be a fingerprint masquerading as an identity. Digests are additionally used for integrity, replay and deterministic evidence — the graph digest and the run identity — and neither of those is ever treated as a constitutional identity.
$derived_counters_comment: Counters whose value is a population of a declared adapter's objects. Declared here so the engine names no adapter: it loops over these records and counts. Adding a counter of this shape is an append, and the engine gains no branch.
